predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The definition inserts a factor 1/T: Cal_T^D = Σ_p (1/T Σ_t x_t(p)) D(ν_p,p). This makes Cal an average error, but every subsequent result treats Cal as a total error. Lemma 2.2 equates FullSwapReg (which has no 1/T) with Cal, and theorems state bounds of the form Cal ≤ εT, which would be vacuous for large T under the normalized definition. The proof of Corollary C.5 also uses Σ_p Σ_t x_t(p)=T, confirming the 1/T factor is spurious.

Claim C.3 states Cal_T^{||·||^2}(x) − 2 Cal_T^{||·||^2}(x̃) ≥ (2 diam^2/H^2) T, but the proof immediately proves the opposite inequality: it writes the difference and bounds it above by 2Σ||p−p̃||^2 ≤ 2T diam^2/H. The main proof then uses the claim in the form Cal ≤ 2 Cal_tilde + 2diam^2 T/H^2, which is the reverse implication. The sign is wrong, and the exponent of H is inconsistent between the claim and the proof.

The abstract claims that for the simplex and ℓ1 norm, the paper obtains ε-calibrated forecasts after T = exp(O(log d/ε)) = d^{O(1/ε)} rounds, 'significantly improving' on [Pen25]. This is not supported by the paper's formal results. Corollary C.5 gives T ≥ (1/ε)^{O(log d/ε^2)} = exp(O(log d · log(1/ε)/ε^2)), which is at best d^{O(log(1/ε)/ε^2)} and is not exp(O(log d/ε)). The Section 1.1 bullet also says the same bound 'recovers' [Pen25], not improves on it.

The bullet states (1/ε)^{O(log d/ε^2)} = d^{O(1/ε^2)}. This equality is false: the left side equals exp(O(log d · log(1/ε)/ε^2)) = d^{O(log(1/ε)/ε^2)}, with an extra unbounded log(1/ε) factor that is not absorbed by O(1/ε^2).

Theorem 4.3 states the lower bound for T ≤ exp(c · min{d^{1/7}, ε^{-1/6}}), but Theorem 4.1, the proof of Theorem 4.3, and the introductory Theorem 1.4 all use min{d^{1/14}, ε^{-1/6}}. The d-exponent is inconsistent and changes the stated lower bound.

The abstract claims that any algorithm requires T ≥ exp(Ω(1/ε)) (assuming d ≥ poly(1/ε)) and that the lower bound is tight. The proven Theorem 4.3 only rules out T ≤ exp(c min{d^{1/14}, ε^{-1/6}}); for large d the strongest consequence is T ≥ exp(Ω(ε^{-1/6})), not exp(Ω(1/ε)). Moreover the upper bound has exponent O(log d · log(1/ε)/ε^2), so the claimed tightness is not established.

The paper uses the negative entropy R(x)=Σ x_i log x_i on the simplex with 'range ρ=log d' to obtain the simplex calibration result. But the formal Rate(P,‖·‖) defined in Section 2.4 requires the Bregman divergence to be bounded by ρ. For negative entropy, D_R(y‖p)=KL(y‖p), which is unbounded when p lies on the boundary and y has positive mass off that face. Thus negative entropy does not satisfy the theorem's stated assumptions, and the claimed recovery of the simplex bound is not justified.

The proof says 'diam_{‖·‖∞}(P')=1' for P'=[-1,1]^{d'}. The ℓ∞ diameter of the cube [-1,1]^{d'} is 2, since the points -1 and 1 differ by 2 in one coordinate. This affects the constant in Lemma 4.2 and the claimed contradiction.

The proof applies Lemma 4.2 with P'=[-1,1]^{d'} and then claims a contradiction to Theorem 4.1. But Theorem 4.1 is a lower bound only for algorithms whose actions lie in the special subset X⊂[-1,1]^d, not for algorithms allowed to play arbitrary points of the full cube. The proof should instead instantiate Lemma 4.2 with P'=X (or otherwise justify how the full-cube algorithm contradicts the X-restricted lower bound), which it does not do.

After deriving the bound, the proof says that choosing L=12ρ/ε and H=diam(P)/√ε guarantees Cal ≤ εT. Substituting into the displayed bound (6ρT)/L + (2 diam^2 T)/H^2 gives εT/2 + 2εT = 2.5εT, not εT. Also Theorem C.1 gives FullSwapReg_T ≤ Tρ/L for BTL, while the proof uses T·3ρ/L; these constants are not reconciled.
